title: Awareness: November men's health, PSA talk and prostate MRI

slides.title: When to ask about a PSA test.
items: Age 50 for most men, says the American Cancer Society.
Age 45 for Black men, or if your father or brother had prostate cancer before 65. Age 40 if more than one did.
55 to 69: the U.S. task force calls it a personal choice to make with your doctor.
slides.footnote: Guidelines differ. Urologists (AUA) say 45 to 50, or 40 to 45 at higher risk. Sources: American Cancer Society; AUA/SUO 2023; USPSTF 2018 (update in progress).

slides.title: If your PSA comes back high.
steps: Usually the first step, through your doctor.
Can show whether a biopsy is needed, and where to look.
PI-RADS 1 to 5 helps you and your urologist plan next steps.
slides.footnote: Source: AUA/SUO guideline, 2023: MRI may be used before a first biopsy and should be done before a repeat biopsy.

slides.title: Clear answers, close to home.
cards: self-pay, PI-RADS report and OnQ AI map
slides.footnote: Read by a board-certified radiologist. The AI supports the read, it doesn't replace it. No referral needed for self-pay.

slides.title: Before your prostate MRI
items: Bring your recent PSA results, if you have them.
Tell us about any implant, pacemaker or metal in your body.
Your doctor may advise no ejaculation for 3 days before.
Arrive 15 minutes early for forms and safety screening.
slides.footnote: Source: U.S. FDA, MRI benefits and risks.

captions.gbp:
November is men's health month, and a good time to ask your doctor one question: should I have a PSA test? The American Cancer Society says start that conversation at 50 for most men, at 45 for Black men or men whose father or brother had prostate cancer before 65, and at 40 if more than one close relative did. Urologists (AUA) suggest 45 to 50, or 40 to 45 at higher risk, and the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force calls screening at 55 to 69 a personal choice to make with your doctor. Guidelines differ, so decide together. If your PSA comes back high, a prostate MRI can help show whether a biopsy is needed and where to look; the AUA guideline says MRI may be used before a first biopsy. Advanced Medical Imaging offers prostate MRI with a PI-RADS report and the OnQ AI risk map, read by a board-certified radiologist, for $495 self-pay. It takes about 45 minutes, uses no radiation, and results go to your urologist in 48 to 72 hours. 3T MRI in St. Petersburg, 1.5T in Seminole. With insurance, a doctor's order is needed. Using Medicare? Ask us what applies.

Book online at advancedimg.com. General information, not medical advice.

facts_checked: 2026-11-05: USPSTF prostate cancer screening (final 2018: 55-69 Grade C individual decision; 70+ Grade D; update in progress, no draft posted); American Cancer Society screening recommendations (discussion at 50 average risk, 45 for African American men or father/brother diagnosed <65, 40 for more than one first-degree relative diagnosed early); AUA/SUO Early Detection of Prostate Cancer 2023 (Stmt 4 baseline PSA 45-50; Stmt 5 40-45 at increased risk; Stmt 13 MRI may be used before initial biopsy; Stmt 30 MRI should be obtained before repeat biopsy; Stmt 14 PI-RADS); U.S. FDA MRI benefits and risks (no ionizing radiation, implant screening). amiweb bbc2313: prices.ts onq $495 both centers; services-data.ts onq-prostate (about 45 min, PI-RADS 1-5, OnQ AI enhances not replaces the read, 48-72 h to urologist, prep: PSA results, implants, avoid ejaculation 3 days if advised, arrive 15 min early, self-pay no referral, insurance needs order).
